**1B.6 Research Note: Srettha Thavisin in 2024**

I did not find credible 2024 evidence that Srettha Thavisin had to resist allied, proxy, client, or domestic-faction proliferation pressure, or that he tolerated proliferation for short-term political gain. What I found instead is consistent anti-proliferation and de-escalation behavior by Thailand’s foreign ministry under his government.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Thailand’s official line under Srettha’s government supported strengthening and transparency in nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament, explicitly aiming at the total elimination of nuclear weapons](https://mfa.go.th/en/content/arfismonnpd-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | May 3, 2024 | https://mfa.go.th/en/content/arfismonnpd-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Thailand publicly aligned itself with non-proliferation and disarmament, which is the closest direct evidence that the government was not enabling proliferation for short-term political interests. | `1B.6`, `1B.1` |

| [ASEAN Foreign Ministers’ Statement on the Escalation of Conflicts in Myanmar](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | April 18, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/asean-fm-statement-escalation-conflicts-myanmar?menu=5d5bd3dc15e39c306002ab1c&page=5d5bd3cb15e39c306002a9ac | Thailand joined ASEAN’s call for restraint, cessation of violence, and humanitarian access in Myanmar. That is de-escalatory conduct, not support for proxy proliferation or militarized escalation. | `1B.6`, `1B.5` |
| [Thailand stresses the importance of upscaling humanitarian assistance along the Thai-Myanmar border at the Human Rights Council](https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c) | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | March 4, 2024 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/vfm010324-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683c | Thailand emphasized humanitarian assistance, dialogue, reconciliation, and a peaceful, stable Myanmar. This is consistent with resisting factional or proxy militarization. | `1B.6`, `1B.5` |

**Search gap**
- I found no credible 2024 evidence that allies, proxies, clients, or domestic factions were pushing proliferation in Thailand, nor that Srettha had to block such efforts.
- I also found no evidence of Thailand enabling proliferation for short-term political advantage.
- The record is therefore best read as a non-proliferation continuity story, not as a case of active internal resistance to an identified proliferation push.
